title: EMV Chip Data Example
applicability: Applies to Element 189 (EMV Chip Data Length) and Element 190 (EMV Chip Data) in EMV transactions.
source: docs/specs/extracted_text.txt Appendix R-1 (chip data example) and Elements 189/190 (field definitions Appendix R exemplifies)
scopeNote: Appendix R's own text states it is a non-exhaustive illustrative example ("The below table does not contain complete list of tags. For complete list of EMV tags, please contact your BUYPASS representative"), so no BR here depends on a closed tag catalog. All seven BRs below are generic structural/processing rules stated by Element 189/190's own definitions, which Appendix R's worked example illustrates.

businessRequirements.title: Element 189 (EMV Chip Data Length) and Element 190 (EMV Chip Data) shall be present whenever the transaction is an EMV transaction.
EMV Chip Data Length shall be exactly three numeric digits (000-999) and shall equal the actual encoded byte count of the following EMV Chip Data value.

A producer field containing a packed-BCD byte-count prefix before EMV TLV bytes must declare whether the prefix belongs to Element 189 framing or the Element 190 value; without an explicit adapter boundary, the candidate remains REVIEW_REQUIRED.
EMV Chip Data shall decompose cleanly into binary Tag/Length/Value sub-elements per Element 190's tag-length encoding rules, with no truncated field and no leftover bytes.
The Application Identifier (tag 9F06) or Dedicated File Name (tag 84) shall be included in EMV Chip Data.
PAN (tag 5A) and Track 2 equivalent data (tag 57) shall not be included in EMV Chip Data.
If a tag appears more than once in EMV Chip Data, it shall resolve to the last value present on the card-to-terminal interface during the transaction.
EMV chip values such as authorized amount, transaction type, currency, and terminal country shall agree with the Segment 100 transaction context.

testDataReadinessSummary.note: The existing Appendix R predicates remain covered by the oracle and tests. The packed-prefix candidate has a deterministic mismatch failure and a matching review-only case; its producer field boundary is not certified. Cross-field checks remain review-required and cryptogram authenticity remains external-fixture-required.

testDataStatus: AppendixREmvChipDataOracle preserves strict bare-TLV validation and adds an explicit packed-BCD-prefix candidate path. It checks the prefix against the following payload byte count and parses the trailing TLV body, but a matching candidate remains REVIEW_REQUIRED until a producer adapter declares the prefix boundary. Existing bounded checks cover EMV-transaction field presence, Element 189 byte count, TLV decomposition, mandatory AID/DF-name, prohibited PAN/Track-2 tags, and duplicate-tag review. Cross-field agreement remains REVIEW_REQUIRED; cryptogram authenticity is external-fixture-required.
remaining: Confirm whether producer adapters may include a packed-BCD length prefix inside their Element 190 field or must provide it separately as Element 189 framing; only then may a matching prefix candidate be promoted beyond REVIEW_REQUIRED.

Resolve cross-field agreement between decoded EMV tag values and Segment 100 context (amount, currency, transaction type, terminal country) if a concrete formula is ever specified by SME input - not stated in Appendix R or Element 189/190 today.
If cryptogram authenticity validation is ever required, source it from a certified EMV kernel/HSM, not AI generation.
Appendix R itself states its tag list is not complete; if a closed EMV tag catalog is ever required, it must come from BUYPASS directly, not be inferred from this appendix.
